ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing (as amended); Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering Law; Law No. 159 of 1981 on Companies (as amended by Law No. 177 of 2020); Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment; Cabinet Decree No. 58 of 2020 on Beneficial Ownership; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) AML/CFT regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Passport Copies of All Shareholders, Directors, and Ultimate Beneficial Owners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit official lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions, FATF public lists, OFAC SDN list, and recognized international PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons and family members/close associates. Suspicious transaction reports must be filed with the Egyptian FIU where indicators are detected. All KYC documentation from foreign jurisdictions must be consular-legalized and translate into Arabic by a licensed translator.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Invest in Egypt online portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be in the Arabic script and is the legally recognized name for the commercial register. A Latin-script transliteration may be registered as an additional name for banking, trade, and international contracting, provided it is a phonetic equivalent of the Arabic name. The use of foreign words is permissible only where not contrary to public order and where the name in Arabic script remains demonstrably distinctive.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or its authorized legal representative may file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a legal memorandum, the original rejection notice, evidence of trademark registration or IP rights where applicable, and a reasoned justification of distinctiveness. The committee must issue a decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, a further application may be made before the Administrative Court (State Council) within 60 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. A physical registered address in Egypt is mandatory for the LLC's principal place of business and service of process. For the specified digital data-pipeline activity, GAFI and the Commercial Registry may accept a virtual-office or regulated co-working space address for pre-incorporation registration, subject to the provider confirming an actual postal address and access to physical inspection. A dedicated brick-and-address must be established within the first operational year for tax, labor, and continuity purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% (Medium-High) — GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Commercial Registry conduct unannounced on-site visits, particularly for non-resident-owned LLCs in the data and technology sector, within the first two years of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egypt Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended (particularly Articles 2 and 47–77 for limited liability companies), read together with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; GAFI one-stop-shop procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration and Commercial Registry (integrated with the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Commercial Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (incorporation document) together with statutory forms (Form 1 and Form 2) and a capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC minimum paid-up capital is EGP 50,000 (unless a special GAFI tech exemption applies). The capital must be fully deposited into an escrow/pre-incorporation bank account opened in the company's name before registration; the blocked amount may not be withdrawn until the Commercial Registry certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution — [EG_LLC]. Resolved, by consent in writing of all members of the Board of Directors, that: (1) the subscription of the entire authorized capital, as set out in the registered Memorandum of Association, is hereby accepted; (2) the registered premises located at [Address], Cairo, Egypt, are adopted as the statutory registered office of the company; (3) Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with authority to act; (4) the CEO is authorized to execute all post-registration filings, tax registrations, and bank account operations; and (5) the company shall not commence revenue operations until the tax card, civil defense clearance, and any required sector licensing are secured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Corporate Registration One-Stop Shop / GAFI digital portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the GAFI digital portal or physical one-stop shop. Provide three optional Arabic/English names and the exact corporate object (web scraping and API data gateway). The system checks for conflicts with registered trademarks/business names in the Commercial Registry. Pay the name reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founding partners
Letter stating the proposed corporate object in Arabic
Lease contract of the intended registered office (or preliminary lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file a written objection to the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 5 business days and propose alternative names; the committee issues a binding ruling within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Pre-Incorporation Capital Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (subject to Central Bank of Egypt anti-money laundering rules)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the name reservation certificate and draft memorandum to the bank's corporate branch; open a temporary account under the proposed company name; deposit the minimum paid-up capital (EGP 50,000) or all agreed capital; request the bank's capital deposit certificate to be attached to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association signed by partners
Passport copies and KYC forms for beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account for enhanced KYC, provide source-of-wealth declarations within 5 business days; if the depositor is non-resident, submit a foreign exchange approval from the Central Bank of Egypt (or the bank's compliance department); appeal to the bank's internal committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Dar El Tawthiq) of the Ministry of Justice in Cairo or the Governorate of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Summon all founding partners before the notary; each must sign the Arabic-language Memorandum of Association (including corporate form LLC, object, capital, registered office, and management); the notary authenticates capacity and signatures; certified copies are issued.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of all partners
Draft indices and flag pages of the Memorandum of Association
Power of attorney if a legal representative executes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags an inconsistent object clause, amend the Memorandum of Association by supplementary notarized deed and re-submit for stamping; if signature authenticity is queried, provide additional identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation bundle: notarized Memorandum of Association (original plus four copies), capital deposit certificate, lease contract registered with municipal tax office, statutory declaration of compliance, and Form 2 (appointment of officers). Pay the GAFI fees through the treasury receipt window. GAFI reviews the company name, objects, capital, and officers for legislative compliance.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered lease contract for the registered office
Form 2 (appointment of the CEO and CFO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a corrective query, supply the missing filings or amended memorandum within 14 calendar days; if GAFI rejects the incorporation, appeal to the GAFI Board of Grievances within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry Office for the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI approval, the file is automatically transferred to the Commercial Registry. The registry official stamps the Memorandum of Association and issues the Commercial Registry certificate (Shahadat Al-Sharikat) including the registry number, incorporation date, and paid-up capital. Collect and verify all details.
required_dossiers: GAFI approval notice with file number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry detects a discrepancy in capital, deposit, or object, re-submit the corrected resolution to GAFI and request a new registry memo; a formal objection to the Commercial Registry Committee is also available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Egyptian Tax Authority Registration (Tax Card and VAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Corporate Tax and VAT Registration Windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a tax registration form using the commercial registry certificate. Obtain the corporate tax card. Register for VAT if annual turnover reaches EGP 500,000 (or elect voluntary registration). Complete electronic invoicing registration on ETA's portal.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Chief Executive Officer's identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA demands an inspection to confirm the physical address, schedule via the ETA call center; if tax classification is disputed, file an internal objection and appeal to the Tax Appeal Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) – Employer Registration Department; Ministry of Manpower – Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the employer registration file to obtain the NOSI number and labor office affiliation. File the initial list of employees and workplace safety declaration. This is essential for payroll, salary distribution, and end-of-service benefits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI disputes employee dates or compensation, provide additional payslip and labor contract evidence; appeal to NOSI's internal grievance committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense Clearance and Occupational Safety Inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Defense Directorate (Ministry of Interior) and Ministry of Manpower – Occupational Safety and Health Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office lease and floor plan to the Civil Defense office to inspect fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and alarm systems; coordinate a physical inspection by an occupational safety and health (OSH) inspector for workplace clearance. Obtain the Civil Defense certificate (required for operating the premises).
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association and commercial registry certificate
Name and identity of the fire safety warden
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection fails, remedy fire and safety defects within 5 working days and apply for re-inspection; if the building's structural load is questioned, obtain a licensed engineer's report and re-submit to the municipal authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Industrial Development Authority (IDA); not applicable for pure information technology services under ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required for public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways; optional telecom/communications license would apply only if the company operates as a public telecommunications service provider under NTRA regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Exempt (professional/information technology service, no industrial establishment under Law 4 of 1994; only an environmental compliance file for office waste is required).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no manufacturing discharge or stationary emissions; office electronic waste disposal must comply with EEAA hazardous waste management rules; indoor noise and power standards per Egyptian building code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Directorate fire safety clearance for the registered office; structural load approval from the municipal authority; Ministry of Manpower occupational safety and health clearance, including minimum workplace ergonomics, fire escape routes, and emergency equipment inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Cairo — official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance platform: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and an official Tax Card from the ETA within 30 days of commercial registration or of the commencement of taxable activity. The LLC must appoint a tax representative registered with the Egyptian Accountants Syndicate under a notarized power of attorney, and file through the ETA's integrated e-filing portal. Required documentation: incorporation certificate from the Commercial Registry (under Companies Law No. 4 of 2018 and, where applicable, GAFI registration), articles of association evidencing unlimited foreign ownership, activity license or a written confirmation that no license is required for the web-scraping/proxy-API activity, address and lease proof, opening balance sheet, and identity documents of directors. VAT registration, which is separate from the income-tax file, is mandatory once annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, with the VAT certificate accessible in the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and is taxed on worldwide net income at the 22.5% corporate headline rate. There is no pass-through regime, no check-the-box treatment, and no territorial remittance exemption for Egyptian-source derived foreign revenue; losses may be carried forward for five years with no carryback.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to US check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections: entity classification is statutory and non-elective. Available elections are administrative and tax-filing options only: (i) voluntary VAT registration before reaching the EGP 500,000 threshold; (ii) adoption of the simplified/small-taxpayer presumptive income regime under the Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020 where the statutory turnover cap is met; and (iii) formal submission of the Article 12 VAT zero-rating declaration for each export service contract, which is accepted by the ETA on a contract-by-contract basis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Egyptian Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, a full VAT/GST-style regime covering goods and services, including digital and data-related services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory VAT registration within 30 days of exceeding the threshold; voluntary registration permitted below it; the threshold is measured on Egyptian-supply turnover, not export turnover).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) is mandatory for VAT registrants: every B2B invoice must be digitally signed using the taxpayer's ETA-issued certificate, submitted for real-time validation through the EIS REST/JSON API, and retained with the ETA smart-code/QR digital stamp. Non-conforming XML/JSON is rejected before issuance, meaning the invoice number is legally ineffective for VAT deduction. Export invoices must carry the 'EX' type code and be correlated with the NAFEZA customs declaration or, for pure software/API services, with the ITIDA IT-export certificate; B2C sales are progressively covered by the mandatory e-receipt system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The Egyptian LLC may zero-rate exported services under Article 12 of the VAT Law and its Executive Regulations where all cumulative conditions are satisfied: (i) the recipient is a non-resident with no Egyptian permanent establishment; (ii) the scraping/API-data services are wholly consumed outside Egypt and are not linked to Egyptian taxable supply; (iii) a written export service contract defines the offshore recipient and jurisdiction of use; and (iv) payment is received in freely convertible foreign currency through an Egyptian licensed bank. The ETA requires either the ITIDA software/IT export certificate or an equivalent service-dispatch dossier (delivery logs, IP evidence, cloud data-center location) to confirm genuine offshore consumption. Note that Stripe-based settlement must ultimately be credited (net of PSP fees) to the LLC's Egyptian bank account and evidenced by a bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate; direct offshore Stripe holding or USDC/crypto settlement is not a recognized repatriation corridor and will defeat the zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export e-invoice issued through the ETA EIS carrying the 'EX' zero-rating code and QR smart stamp, cross-referenced to the export contract
Signed export service contract and service-level agreement identifying the non-resident customer and defining offshore consumption of the scraping-API gateway

NAFEZA Customs Export Declaration — required only where physical media, servers, or co-located hardware accompany the service supply; for pure digital service exports, replaced by the ITIDA software/IT export certificate
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (for tangible payloads) or, for digital services, hosting-provider delivery logs and IP-address evidence demonstrating consumption outside Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian authorized bank evidencing foreign-currency receipts in USD/EUR and crediting to the LLC's Egyptian account
Stripe payout/settlement reports reconciled to the IRC, board resolution approving the export pricing, and the LLC's VAT export registration record in the ETA exporter database
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may reassess zero-rated supplies for five years (ten years in cases of fraud or deliberate concealment). Where the offshore-consumption or foreign-currency repatriation trail cannot be substantiated, the export is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply at 14% VAT, the refund is clawed back, and the tax is collected with the statutory late-payment addition. Fraudulent zero-rating claims carry severe legal consequences: criminal prosecution under the VAT Law with imprisonment (up to five years) and monetary fines scaled to the evaded amount, mandatory re-issuance of corrected e-invoices, removal from the exporter VAT-refund fast-track, and reputational referral under Egypt's anti-money-laundering framework. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the CBE deadline also exposes the LLC to a deemed-distribution adjustment at 22.5% corporate income tax, and USDC/cryptocurrency settlement is not a valid method of satisfying Egyptian exchange-control and VAT-documentation requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — primary regulator under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and the Foreign Exchange (Exchange Control) Law No. 97 of 1976, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has operated a CBE-supervised flexible exchange-rate regime since the 6 March 2024 currency unification, with the EGP price formed by interbank supply and demand. Current-account flows (software subscriptions, API access, and data services) are convertible for bona fide commercial purposes if the underlying contract, commercial invoice, and economic substance satisfy the receiving bank's documentary review. Capital-account flows, including dividend remittances and capital repatriation, are permitted only after inward FDI has been registered with the CBE/GAFI and the company demonstrates current tax clearance (Tax Law No. 91 of 2024, VAT Law No. 67 of 2016) and audited financial statements. Practical profit-remittance hurdles include heightened AML documentation, a statutory prohibition on cryptocurrency-denominated settlement inside Egypt, and bank-level FX-liquidity allocation, which can delay large on-demand USD transfers during periods of balance-of-payments stress.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Exchange Control Law No. 97 of 1976, export proceeds — including digital, data-service, and licensing revenue — must be repatriated into a licensed Egyptian bank account in the original invoice currency, within the contractual credit period generally capped at 180 days. There is currently no statutory percentage surrender requirement: the temporary mandatory conversion ratios (in the range of 80–100% of proceeds) applied during the 2022–2023 FX-scarcity episodes were withdrawn by the CBE's 6 March 2024 flexible-exchange-rate reform. Exporters may retain the full balance in foreign-currency current accounts for permitted operational, hedging, or liquidation purposes, subject to CBE transaction-code filings and documentary retention by the account-holding bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (EGP + USD); Share-Capital Custody/Incorporation Deposit Account
Operational Current Account (EGP + USD); Share-Capital Custody/Incorporation Deposit Account
Operational Current Account (EGP + USD); Share-Capital Custody/Incorporation Deposit Account
Multi-Currency Foreign-Currency Account + EGP Operational Account; Share-Capital Custody/Incorporation Deposit Account
Operational Current Account (EGP + USD); Share-Capital Custody/Incorporation Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. Offshore digital EMI providers (Wise, Airwallex, M-DAQ, etc.) are not licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt and cannot substitute for the statutory Egyptian bank account required for LLC incorporation, export-proceeds repatriation, FX clearance, or tax registration. They may be used only as auxiliary collection/disbursement rails for immaterial, non-trade flows; all official treasury flows must clear through a CBE-licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is de facto mandatory for foreign-owned LLCs. The Egyptian AML framework (Law No. 80 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations) and CBE KYC directives require the authorized signatory (general manager or director) to appear physically at the branch for a compliance interview; remote or video-only account opening is not granted on a standard basis. The ultimate beneficial owner may delegate to a local signatory under a notarized, apostilled, and legally accepted power of attorney, provided the full UBO chain is documented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO located abroad holding the LLC through a multi-tier foreign parent chain; ownership transparency questioned by the bank's MLRO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO attestation (Art. 86, AML Law No. 80/2016); certified registry extracts for each intermediate entity; ownership percentage schedule; passport and residency proof of all natural persons; source-of-wealth/source-of-funds statements; bank references from the parent-company account; apostilled board resolution appointing the Egyptian signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business line characterized as 'web scraping / data brokering' with high intangible cross-border revenue and no physical-trade evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed API/SaaS subscription agreements; customer identification schedule; platform utilization and delivery-traffic reports; privacy-policy and data-source compliance documentation; incident-response and breach-notification framework; a local Egyptian sponsor or service agreement evidencing substance; prior-period invoice ledger and payment receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Target payment rails reference 'Cryptocurrency_USDC' — crypto settlement is treated as unlawful/unlicensed under Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE practice, creating a hard compliance rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming that all crypto-denominated receivables are converted into fiat through a licensed foreign exchange and arrive in Egypt solely as fiat SWIFT credits; corporate policy prohibiting crypto settlement within the Egyptian banking perimeter; bank statements proving only fiat funding; contractual omnibus clause requiring customers to pay in fiat currency on the Egyptian books.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Parent-company equity injection is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's regulated bank to the LLC's CBE-licensed Egyptian bank, classified under the BoP/CBE purpose code for direct-investment equity capital (FDI registration). The wire narration must reference the LLC commercial-register number, the GAFI investment file, and the share-capital custody account; funds may not be introduced via crypto rails, cash deposits, or third-party payment wallets. After inward settlement, the bank issues the FDI credit advice and the CBE registration anchor required for future dividend or capital repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border service payments (proxy infrastructure, sub-processors, SaaS licensing, bandwidth) are cleared via SWIFT MT103 messages carrying the appropriate CBE service-transaction purpose code, supported by the signed services agreement, commercial invoice, and delivery evidence. Commercial Letters of Credit (sight/usance L/C) are used only for physical hardware procurement (server purchase, network equipment) where the CBE goods-import framework applies; electronic-service imports do not require L/C. Stripe/global-payout proceeds are consolidated and swept to the Egyptian USD account through the international SWIFT network, then converted into EGP only when operational needs require.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/EGP) supported by an identified underlying service-export receivable with tenor aligned to the invoice date
FX swaps (USD/EGP or USD/EUR) for short-term working-capital timing adjustment within the bank's net-open-position limits
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) transacted onshore through a CBE-licensed bank when onshore deliverable liquidity is scarce and the underlying exposure is documented
Cross-currency interest-rate/principal swaps (USD/EUR vs. EGP) for long-horizon balance-sheet hedging, subject to CBE transaction approval and bank credit appetite

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 8) with audited financial statements and full tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the fourth month after the fiscal year end (e.g., 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers); any extension per ETA publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment surcharge of 2.5% of unpaid tax (capped at 50%); 10% late-filing penalty on the due tax under Article 138; criminal liability for wilful non-filing or fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, shareholder register extract, and GAFI annual file confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months following the fiscal year end; any shareholding or statutory register change must be notified within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late filing surcharges; suspension of GAFI certificate of good standing; blocking of commercial transactions and import/export operations; administrative strike-off after repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Justice - Commercial Registry Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prohibition on concluding commercial contracts; inability to open or maintain corporate bank accounts; judicial penalties under Commercial Registration Law and eventual deregistration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit for every LLC under the Companies Law regardless of size; tax law additionally requires certified audited statements when gross annual revenue exceeds EGP 500,000 or when the enterprise claims carried-forward losses
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), nationally issued and IFRS-aligned, with full IFRS required for listed companies; tax accounting separately governed by Law 91/2005 records obligations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Real beneficiary (UBO) register must be filed with GAFI and confirmed annually alongside the annual corporate return; any share transfer, addition, or removal of a natural-person beneficial owner requires a mandatory update within 30 days of the transaction
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assembly and Manager/Board resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free-zone companies may apply 0% corporate income tax on qualifying activity subject to an annual 5% license fee. Investment Law 72/2017 permits a deduction of up to 50% of investment capital for eligible licensed projects, and the Supreme Council for Investment may grant additional cost deductions for strategic projects.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 50) filed through the Egypt Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing system; paper filing requires prior ETA approval.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with quarterly provisional tax payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within four months after the close of the taxable fiscal year (e.g., 31 December year-end returns due 30 April). Quarterly advance tax payments are due within 15 days after the end of each fiscal quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Egyptian tax ID, registered address, and fiscal year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian branch/PE tax ID and address of the authorised tax representative in Egypt; no foreign business licence number is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting identity: audited financial statement standard, income tax law articles used, related party disclosure flag
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate 'PE as separate taxable entity' and attach Egyptian-audited financial statements prepared in EGP for the permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, invoiced sales, and service income before deducting cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source revenue attributable to the PE or generated through the Egyptian commerce-scraping API platform's local servers and contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only costs borne by the Egyptian PE and supported by invoices, bank transfers, and contracts; cross-border costs must be allocated under ETA TP rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses, hosting fees, marketing, salaries, and depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred for the production of Egyptian taxable income; a 50% cap on head-office allocated overheads applies under Law 91/2005 unless a DTA provides otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss relief (net after all deductible expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Always show the PE's separately computed profit; a non-resident cannot merge head-office income into this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses carried forward (maximum five years)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses of the Egyptian PE; foreign branch losses are not available for set-off against Egyptian PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If zero, enter 0 and attach supporting loss computation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT liability at the 22.5% statutory rate, less quarterly provisional payments already made
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate tax on net PE profit only; attach proof of all quarterly ETA payment receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits on Egyptian-source income previously subjected to WHT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach ETA withholding forms issued by Egyptian payers; WHT credit is final and cannot be refunded unless a treaty/domestic rule permits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EGP 1,000 per month or fraction thereof, capped at EGP 20,000 under Tax Procedure Law 206/2020; late tax payment triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of the unpaid tax. Failure to file for a period exceeding 60 days from the deadline may lead to estimated assessment and an additional penalty of 5% of assessed tax; erroneous or fraudulent statements expose the taxpayer to criminal fines and imprisonment as provided in Law 91/2005 and the Tax Procedure Law.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on cash and in-kind dividends paid to non-resident shareholders under Law 91/2005 Article 58, subject to treaty reduction
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the Egypt-Egypt residence jurisdiction's DTA reduced rate, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence; (2) file ETA Form for withholding tax relief with the Egyptian Tax Authority before payment; (3) submit the TRC, a statement of beneficial ownership, and proof of no PE in Egypt; and (4) obtain an ETA clearance notification confirming the reduced WHT rate. Retroactive relief is possible by filing an amended withholding return and refund claim where the treaty reference in the ETA portal is accurately completed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic rates: 20% on royalties for intellectual property, 20% on interest paid to non-residents, and 20% on payments for management/technical services. Under most Egyptian DTAs, royalty and interest rates are reduced to 10-15% subject to beneficial ownership and the absence of a PE. Egyptian-source rental payments for real estate are also 20%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 15,000,000 for controlled transactions (Local File requirement); Master File required when Egyptian entity participates in a multinational group whose consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 500,000,000; Country-by-Country Report required where consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EGP 8,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not administer a GCC-style ESR regime. Instead, economic substance is assessed under Law 91/2005 anti-avoidance provisions, specifically Article 103 on sham transactions, and under the Tax Procedure Law 206/2020. A recipient of treaty benefits must satisfy the beneficial-ownership and active-business-substance tests. For free-zone licensed LLCs, substantive local activity (employees, premises, decision-making, and revenue generation) must be observable; otherwise the tax authority may reclassify free-zone income as taxable head-office income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Egyptian-source revenues, forgery of invoices, using off-book bank accounts, or omitting related-party transactions in Form 50 with intent to evade CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of evaded tax plus a fine equal to 100% of the evaded amount; penalty under Tax Procedure Law 206/2020 can reach EGP 2,000,000 for corporate entities; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of controlling officers for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who sign false returns or direct the concealment can be made jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt. Travel bans and asset freezing orders are routinely issued under the law when evasion exceeds substantial thresholds; repeat offenders face imprisonment without the option of a fine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating an Egyptian LLC to route intercompany commissions, host an API endpoint, or hold a free-zone licence without real employees, premises, bank activity, or business risk, and without commercial substance supporting the claimed revenue allocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A reclassification of the entity as a non-taxable sham or transparent conduit; recapture of the 0% free-zone rate with CIT at 22.5% on all accumulated profits plus late payment surcharge of 2% per month; penalties up to EGP 500,000 for submission of false substance declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under Law 91/2005 and Companies Law No. 4/2018 when the entity is used to evade tax or manipulate creditor positions. Each director who knowingly facilitated the sham may be ordered to pay evaded tax personally, and the commercial registrar may disqualify them from board positions in Egypt for up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fictitious Intercompany Loans and Interest Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording a shareholder loan from a low-tax jurisdiction with no principal repayment schedule or lender cash-flow evidence, then paying 20% interest to drain the Egyptian taxable base, particularly where the equity injection remains unreported.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the entire interest deduction; back-taxes at 22.5%; 2% monthly late-payment surcharge; additional penalty equal to 10% of the disallowed interest under TP rules; potential WHT assessment at 20% on the interest paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved artificially high interest rates can be held aggregation liable for the resulting tax under the anti-abuse regime; if the structure is deemed a disguised distribution, a 10% dividend WHT is applied to the shareholder-beneficiary, and a director may receive a fine up to double the amount paid by the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving USDC or Stripe-settled API subscription fees via foreign wallets without maintaining a licensed money-handling record, or commingling corporate e-commerce receivables with personal cryptocurrency accounts, thus breaching AML Law No. 80/2002 as amended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EGP 5,000,000 for corporate entities and seizure of compromised assets; supervisory penalties from the Financial Regulatory Authority; prohibited access to the Egyptian banking system for the LLC. Suspicious transaction filings not made to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Unit (EMC) trigger separate administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to establish a beneficial-ownership registry or who knowingly process proceeds of unlicensed scraping activity through crypto rails may be prosecuted personally, with imprisonment from one to seven years and confiscation of personal assets obtained from the offence. Travel bans are standard during the investigation phase.
